description: World origins, the Vanishing, and creatures associated with the lands beneath the clouds.

entries.title: The Shattering of the World
entries.summary: Every people remembers a calamity that broke a once-whole world into floating lands, though their explanations differ.
body: Elven tradition blames the betrayal of celestial Starborn; Dwarven tradition recalls the reality-shaping Heart of the Forge; Human stories describe divine punishment for mortal hubris; Gnomish accounts blame Veldrin Sparkwhistle and a catastrophic engineering error.

Across the contradictory stories, four elements persist: a cosmic or divine force, mortal ambition, the opening of [[the-abyss|the Abyss]], and the rising of shattered land into the sky. No surviving culture can prove which version is true.

sourceRefs.outlineTitle: World Lore / The Shattering of the World

entries.title: The Vanishing
entries.summary: Floating islands can slowly lose the force that holds them aloft and disappear beneath the clouds without warning.
body: The Vanishing begins with cracking land, thinning air, cold winds, and failing sustaining magic. Entire settlements and cultures may descend into [[the-abyss|the Abyss]] and never return.
Fear of loss intensifies competition for stable land, water, food, and defensible routes. Rulers rarely discuss the phenomenon openly, but every island government must reckon with it.

entries.title: UndterWyrms
entries.summary: Ancient serpentine horrors are said to consume islands, airships, and even dragons that fall beneath the clouds.
body: UndterWyrms are described as immense coiled predators woven into the fabric of the Abyss itself. The oldest dragons become guarded when questioned about them, lending weight to stories that they can swallow great wyrms whole.
Whether literal beasts or a cultural explanation for the total loss caused by [[the-vanishing|the Vanishing]], they embody the certainty that little returns from below.

sourceRefs.outlineTitle: The land beneath the clouds / UndterWyrms

entries.title: Beasts of the Abyss
entries.summary: A family of colossal predators, parasites, and warped hunters is reported in the lightless reaches below the clouds.
body: Accounts name the ship-swallowing Abyssal Maw, the storm-making Shadowwing Leviathan, regenerative Sable Tendrils, the web-spinning Blackclaw, the phasing Nightmare Hound, and mounted Gloomriders.

Other reports describe corruption, gravity wells, psychic howls, poisonous attacks, technological decay, and predators able to hide within the darkness. These stories may overlap, exaggerate, or describe distinct Abyssal ecologies.

sections.heading: Legacy Creature Abilities
body: The source presents named supernatural attacks and effects without a unified converted stat framework. Mechanical implementation requires conversion.
